thread:
maya: Heads up — noticed a big drop in GPU-serving metrics in asia-southeast this morning, looks correlated with a flurry of node evictions.
jon: seeing same on dashboards, token-rate dropped ~60% around 08:12 UTC. traces are largely missing for the affected pods. :eyes:
li: alerts fired for kube-proxy restart storms in that region. pods were OOMKilled on several nodes.
ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-4123 - asia-southeast serving degradation (ops-oncall: @infra-oncall)
infra-oncall: digging in — are logs present from the kube-proxy / evicted pods?
maya: logs are sparse, most of the pod logs show up as "logstream unavailable" in the logging UI. metrics exporter only shows up for a subset of nodes.
sergey: this looks like our node-level log agent lost connectivity during the network ejection. I see a transient iptables rule change from the node-provision script in the same window.
jon: any idea why traces are gone too? We rely on the agent to ship traces and metrics.
li: if the log/trace agent couldn't reach OTLP endpoint, the buffering was disabled due to disk pressure config. nodes were under memory pressure so agent likely dropped telemetry.
maya: so two failures: kube-proxy churn causing packet drops + node disk/memory pressure causing telemetry agent to self-throttle. that explains missing metrics and traces.
infra-oncall: moving to containment: 1) stop further ejections by pausing the node-provision job, 2) mark healthy nodes unschedulable for a quick gradual drain, 3) increase agent buffer limits temporarily.
jon: pausing job now: `kubectl -n infra patch cronjob node-provision --patch '{"spec":{"suspend":true}}'`
ops-bot: cronjob/node-provision patched (suspend=true) by jon
li: bumped agent buffer size in DaemonSet to 512Mi and restarted daemonset pods in asia-southeast: `kubectl -n kube-telemetry set env ds/log-agent BUFFER_MAX=512Mi && kubectl rollout restart ds/log-agent -n kube-telemetry -l region=asia-southeast`
sergey: pushing a quick iptables revert to nodes that have the provisioning rule applied, rolling at 5 nodes at a time. using: ```
for node in $(kubectl get nodes -l region=asia-southeast -o name); do ssh $node sudo iptables -D INPUT -m comment --comment "provision-eject"; done
```
maya: after the revert, some metrics started trickling back at 08:27 UTC. full metrics stream not stable yet.
jon: traces are also coming back for a few requests. RTT still high for KV-cache fetches.
li: observed one exporter pod with corrupted checkpoint file — deleted pod + recreated and metrics resumed for that host.
infra-oncall: rolling patch plan: 1) revert provisioning rule (done), 2) increase agent buffer (done), 3) restart corrupt exporter (done), 4) run a small synthetic load to validate no new evictions. scheduling synthetic run in 10m.
maya: quick note — cost impact: fallback to smaller-model replicas triggered in routing for ~20 minutes, estimated extra cost ~ $1.2k due to cross-region burst and smaller-model compute overhead. logging ticket for chargeback.
jon: follow-up: add e2e test in prov job to ensure it doesn't insert network rules without an annotation. also add a canary that validates agent connectivity after node changes.
sergey: opened PR to node-provisioner: add `--require-annotation=provision-allow` before applying net rules.
li: instrumentation fix: change agent to persist buffer to a separate fs mount and keep backpressure tolerant by default. will be a config rollout next week.
maya: temporary mitigation steps worked, metrics/traces fully restored by 09:05 UTC. marking incident as mitigated but keeping oncall watch for 2h. :white_check_mark:
ops-bot: incident INC-2026-4123 status -> mitigated (mitigated_by: maya, jon, li, sergey)
infra-oncall: creating postmortem draft and action-items: prov job hardening, agent buffer persistence, exporter checkpoint validation, cost chargeback calc. assigning owners.
jon: thanks team. if nobody objects, I'll file the follow-up tasks in the infra board.
maya: go for it. thanks all for fast response. :thumbsup:
